memory_candidates.content: When a Lean plan must site a new theorem that joins two sibling modules' vocabularies, resolve the import DAG by TRANSITIVE closure before planning a new module or a new import edge. In BimodalLogic's RaySummary layer, LadderAgree and LadderStepFrag look like disjoint siblings (LadderAgree imports only AnchorLayer + CounterQuotient; LadderStepFrag imports only LadderRealize), yet LadderAgree IS in LadderStepFrag's closure via LadderStepFrag -> LadderRealize -> LadderChain -> LadderPump -> LadderAgree. Reading only the two files' own import lines would have forced a new module, which in this repository additionally owes lake exe mk_all, a module-inventory regeneration and a check-metalogic-cycles.sh allowlist check. The cheap authoring-time confirmation is to assemble the plan's pinned Challenge signatures with a single candidate import and compile them (lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --dry-run --compile): a successful compile proves every referenced declaration resolves from that one import, settling siting mechanically rather than by reading import lines.
